newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault car losses likely worsened in 96 -chairman.
newsitem.headline: Renault car losses likely worsened in 96 -chairman.

text.p: The chairman of French carmaker Renault reiterated on Monday that the group's car division losses were likely to have worsened in 1996.
Renault hoped to bring the loss-making sector back to breakeven in 1997, Louis Schweitzer told Le Figaro newspaper in an interview.
"I do not at this point have definitive information on 1996, but the trend indicates a noticeable worsening of our losses," he said.
"Our target for 1997 is a return to balance in the car division. We hope 1996 will merely be a temporary acccident."
Renault's car division lost 1.71 billion francs ($320 million) in 1995 compared with a positive contribution to operating income of 289 million francs in 1994.
It made an operating loss of 911 million francs in the first half of 1996 compared with a first-half 1995 operating profit of 358 million francs.
Schweitzer said in December that he thought the trend in losses mentioned at the announcement of first-half 1996 results would strengthen due to a price war between manufacturers.
